decisions.reason: This particle-therapy water phantom remains close to the firm's core QA and dosimetry knowledge, so management can keep learning and improving it, although its narrower market keeps withdrawal risk above that of the chamber products.

A small-volume ionization chamber fits directly with the firm's established detector design, calibration, and clinical support capabilities, making continued commercialization and refinement more attractive than exit.

An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is a highly related extension of the firm's existing measurement business, so accumulated user feedback and in-house expertise support keeping it on the market.
A thimble ionization chamber is a standard, well-understood product squarely within the firm's absorptive capacity, so management would be unlikely to discontinue it absent clear failure signals.
